title: Self-adjointness of coordinate noise
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product of probability spaces whose coordinate atom weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$, let $i$ be a coordinate, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on the product outcome space. If $N_{i,\rho}h=h-L_i h+\rho L_i h$, where $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$ and the conditional expectation averages over coordinate $i$, then $\mathbb E_P[(N_{i,\rho}f)g]=\mathbb E_P[f(N_{i,\rho}g)]$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product of coordinate probability spaces
each coordinate atom weight is strictly positive
$f,g$ are real-valued functions on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a coordinate $i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P[(N_{i,\rho}f)g]=\mathbb E_P[fN_{i,\rho}g]$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
